mcqs.stem: Best guess: can the auditor of a public company also perform its internal audit function?

choices.text: Yes, if the audit committee approves the service in advance
choices.explanation: Pre-approval cannot make a prohibited service permissible.

choices.text: Yes, if different staff perform the audit and the internal audit
choices.explanation: Separate staffing does not cure the prohibition.

choices.text: Yes, if the internal audit fees are below the audit fees
choices.explanation: There is no fee-based exception.

choices.text: No; internal audit outsourcing is prohibited for issuers
choices.explanation: Correct. SOX and SEC rules prohibit it.

mcqs.explanation: Internal audit outsourcing is on the SEC's list of prohibited nonaudit services for issuer audit clients.

mcqs.stem: Which service may the auditor of a public company provide if the audit committee pre-approves it?

choices.text: Preparing the corporation's federal income tax return
choices.explanation: Correct. Tax compliance is permitted with pre-approval, subject to PCAOB limits.

choices.text: Valuing an acquired subsidiary's intangible assets
choices.explanation: Valuation services are prohibited.

choices.text: Designing the company's general ledger system
choices.explanation: Financial information systems design is prohibited.

choices.text: Recording the company's routine monthly journal entries
choices.explanation: Bookkeeping is prohibited.

mcqs.explanation: Tax compliance and planning are permitted if pre-approved and not aggressive, contingent, or provided to persons in financial reporting oversight roles.

mcqs.stem: For an issuer audit, how long may the lead engagement partner serve before rotating off, and for how long?

choices.explanation: Correct. Lead and concurring (engagement quality review) partners: 5 on, 5 off.
That applies to other audit partners, not the lead.
The lead partner's time-out is 5 years.
No such rule exists; 1 year is the cooling-off period for employment.

mcqs.explanation: Lead and concurring (engagement quality review) partners: 5 on, 5 off. Other audit partners: 7 on, 2 off.

mcqs.stem: Which is **not** one of the SEC's four principles of auditor independence?

choices.text: The auditor should not audit its own work or judgments
choices.explanation: This is one of the four principles.

choices.text: The auditor should not act as an advocate for the client
choices.explanation: This is one of the four principles.

choices.text: The auditor should not perform management functions
choices.explanation: This is one of the four principles.

choices.text: The auditor should not earn over 15% of revenue from one client
choices.explanation: Correct. This is not an SEC principle.

mcqs.explanation: The four principles: no mutual or conflicting interest, no auditing own work, no management functions, no advocacy.

mcqs.stem: The auditor of an issuer is asked to prepare the personal income tax return of the company's CFO. What is the result?

choices.text: Permitted, with the audit committee's pre-approval
choices.explanation: PCAOB Rule 3523 prohibits tax services to persons in a financial reporting oversight role.

choices.text: Permitted, if the CFO pays the fee personally
choices.explanation: Who pays does not change the prohibition.

choices.text: Impaired; the CFO is in a reporting oversight role
choices.explanation: Correct. Rule 3523 prohibits tax services to persons in a financial reporting oversight role at the audit client (and their immediate family), with narrow exceptions.

choices.text: Permitted, if the return has no aggressive positions
choices.explanation: The prohibition applies to any tax service for the CFO.

mcqs.explanation: Rule 3523 prohibits tax services to persons in a financial reporting oversight role at the audit client (and their immediate family), with narrow exceptions.

mcqs.stem: A senior on the issuer's audit team is hired as the client's CFO. The audit of the following year begins four months after her last work on the engagement. What is the effect?

choices.text: The firm isn't independent; the cooling-off period wasn't met
choices.explanation: Correct. The firm is not independent if a former engagement team member takes a financial reporting oversight role within the one-year cooling-off period.

choices.text: None, because the one-year rule applies only to audit partners
choices.explanation: The cooling-off rule applies to all members of the audit engagement team.

choices.text: She must wait five years before she can join the client
choices.explanation: Five years is the partner rotation time-out, not the cooling-off period.

choices.text: The client's audit committee may waive the rule for her
choices.explanation: The rule cannot be waived by the audit committee.

mcqs.explanation: The firm is not independent if a former engagement team member takes a financial reporting oversight role within the one-year cooling-off period.

mcqs.stem: Under PCAOB Rule 3526, when must the auditor communicate relationships that may bear on independence to the audit committee?

choices.text: Only when a problem with independence is identified
choices.explanation: Communication is required before acceptance and at least annually.

choices.text: Before accepting the engagement, then at least annually
choices.explanation: Correct. Rule 3526: describe in writing all relationships that may reasonably bear on independence, discuss them, document the discussion, and affirm independence.

choices.text: Only at the end of each quarterly review engagement
choices.explanation: Timing is before acceptance and annually, not quarterly.

choices.text: Only when the lead audit partner rotates off
choices.explanation: Rotation is unrelated to this communication.

mcqs.explanation: Rule 3526: describe in writing all relationships that may reasonably bear on independence, discuss them, document the discussion, and affirm independence.

mcqs.stem: Which service is prohibited for an issuer audit client even if the audit committee approves it?

choices.text: A review of the issuer's quarterly financial information
choices.explanation: That review is part of the audit relationship and is permitted.

choices.text: Issuing a comfort letter for a securities offering
choices.explanation: Comfort letters are permitted audit-related services.

choices.text: Actuarial services related to the pension obligation
choices.explanation: Correct. Actuarial services are prohibited.
Tax compliance is permitted with pre-approval.

mcqs.explanation: Actuarial services affecting financial statement amounts are prohibited because the auditor would audit its own work.

mcqs.stem: Under Government Auditing Standards (the Yellow Book), how is the auditor's preparation of a government's financial statements treated?

choices.explanation: The Yellow Book does not ban it outright but treats it as a significant threat.

choices.text: A significant threat to evaluate, document, and safeguard
choices.explanation: Correct. The Yellow Book uses a conceptual framework.

choices.text: Always permitted, without any evaluation or documentation
choices.explanation: The auditor must assess and document the threat.

choices.text: Permitted only if the government has no accounting staff
choices.explanation: The test is management's SKE, not having no staff.

mcqs.explanation: The Yellow Book uses a conceptual framework. Preparing statements creates self-review and management participation threats that must be evaluated and documented.

mcqs.stem: A firm audits a 401(k) plan under ERISA. For Department of Labor purposes, independence is required with respect to:

choices.explanation: DOL independence extends to the plan sponsor as well.

choices.text: The plan and the plan sponsor
choices.explanation: Correct. DOL rules: the accountant must be independent of both the employee benefit plan and the plan sponsor.
Participants are not the attest client.
The funds are not the relevant entities.

mcqs.explanation: DOL rules: the accountant must be independent of both the employee benefit plan and the plan sponsor.

mcqs.stem: A partner (not lead or concurring) has provided significant services on an issuer audit for seven consecutive years. What is required?

choices.text: No rotation is required for non-lead partners
choices.explanation: Other audit partners must rotate after 7 years.
The 5-year time-out applies to lead and concurring partners.
Correct. 7 years on, 2 years off.
One year is the cooling-off period for employment.

mcqs.explanation: Audit partners other than the lead and concurring partners: a maximum of 7 years, then a 2-year time-out.

mcqs.stem: The audit committee of an issuer wants the auditor to provide a tax shelter strategy that relies on a position unlikely to be sustained, for a contingent fee. What is the evaluation?

choices.text: Permitted, with the audit committee's pre-approval
choices.explanation: Pre-approval cannot make an aggressive or contingent-fee tax service acceptable.

choices.text: Prohibited: an aggressive position and a contingent fee
choices.explanation: Correct. PCAOB Rules 3521 and 3522 are both violated.

choices.text: Prohibited only because the fee is contingent
choices.explanation: The aggressive position independently violates Rule 3522.

choices.text: Permitted if disclosed in the proxy statement
choices.explanation: Disclosure does not cure the prohibition.

mcqs.explanation: Rule 3521 bans contingent fees; Rule 3522 bans marketing, planning, or opining on aggressive tax positions and confidential transactions.

mcqs.stem: Which statement about audit committee pre-approval for issuers is correct?

choices.text: Only nonaudit services require audit committee pre-approval
choices.explanation: All audit and permitted nonaudit services require pre-approval.

choices.text: Pre-approval by the committee allows any nonaudit service
choices.explanation: Prohibited services cannot be approved.

choices.text: All audit and permitted nonaudit services need pre-approval
choices.explanation: Correct. SOX Section 202: the audit committee pre-approves all audit and permitted nonaudit services.

choices.text: Management may approve services if the committee delegates to the CFO
choices.explanation: Delegation is only to committee members, not to management.

mcqs.explanation: SOX Section 202: the audit committee pre-approves all audit and permitted nonaudit services. It may delegate to one or more of its own members, not to management.

mcqs.stem: Under SOX §301, who is directly responsible for appointing, compensating and overseeing an issuer's external auditor?

choices.explanation: Correct. The audit committee has direct responsibility for the auditor.
Management doesn't appoint the auditor under SOX.
The PCAOB inspects and sets standards; it doesn't appoint auditors.
Shareholders may ratify, but the committee is responsible.

mcqs.explanation: SOX §301: the audit committee is directly responsible for the appointment, compensation and oversight of the registered public accounting firm.

mcqs.stem: How may an issuer's audit committee preapprove non-audit services under SEC rules?

choices.explanation: Delegation to management isn't allowed.
Correct. Policies must be detailed as to the service and the committee informed of each service.

choices.text: Only after the service is completed
choices.explanation: Preapproval comes before the service.

choices.text: By a general approval of all tax work
choices.explanation: Policies must be detailed by service.

mcqs.explanation: SEC Rule 2-01(c)(7): preapproval may be by specific approval or by detailed policies and procedures, with the committee informed of each service; it can't be delegated to management.

mcqs.stem: An issuer's audit firm prepares the personal tax return of the issuer's CFO, a person in a financial reporting oversight role. Under PCAOB Rule 3523, independence is:

choices.text: Not impaired if the CFO pays the fee
choices.explanation: Who pays the fee doesn't matter.

choices.text: Not impaired with audit committee preapproval
choices.explanation: Preapproval doesn't cure Rule 3523.
Correct. Tax services to persons in a financial reporting oversight role impair independence, with narrow exceptions.

choices.text: Impaired only if the return is aggressive
choices.explanation: Rule 3523 covers routine returns too.

mcqs.explanation: PCAOB Rule 3523: a firm isn't independent if it provides tax services to a person in a financial reporting oversight role at an issuer audit client during the professional engagement period.

mcqs.stem: An issuer's audit firm proposes a fee for tax planning advice that depends on the tax savings achieved. What is the effect?

choices.explanation: Contingent fees are prohibited regardless of approval.

choices.text: Nothing, because tax services are permitted
choices.explanation: The fee structure is the problem.

choices.text: Impaired only above a dollar threshold
choices.explanation: There is no threshold.
Correct. Contingent fee arrangements with an issuer audit client impair independence.

mcqs.explanation: SEC Rule 2-01(c)(5) and PCAOB Rule 3521: a contingent fee arrangement with an audit client impairs independence.

mcqs.stem: How often does the PCAOB inspect a registered firm that audits 100 or fewer issuers?

choices.explanation: Correct. Firms auditing more than 100 issuers are inspected annually.
Annual inspection applies above 100 issuers.
Inspections are regular.
The interval is at least every three years.

mcqs.explanation: SOX §104: annual inspections for firms auditing more than 100 issuers; at least every three years otherwise.

mcqs.stem: For an issuer audit, how long may the lead engagement partner serve before rotating off?

choices.explanation: That was the pre-SOX rule.
Correct. Followed by a 5-year time-out.
The limit is 5 years.
SOX requires rotation.

mcqs.explanation: SEC rules require the lead and concurring partners to rotate after 5 years, with a 5-year time-out.

mcqs.stem: What does SOX Section 407 require an issuer to disclose?

choices.text: The auditor's fees by staff level
choices.explanation: That isn't Section 407.
That isn't Section 407.
Correct. And if not, why not.
That isn't Section 407.

mcqs.explanation: Section 407 requires disclosure of whether at least one audit committee member is a financial expert.

mcqs.stem: Which issuers are exempt from the auditor attestation on ICFR under SOX 404(b)?

choices.explanation: They need auditor attestation.
They generally need it.

choices.text: All issuers in their tenth year
choices.explanation: Not an exemption.
Correct. Management still reports under 404(a).

mcqs.explanation: SOX 404(b) auditor attestation doesn't apply to non-accelerated filers.

mcqs.stem: An audit partner's compensation depends on selling non-audit services to her issuer audit clients. What is the effect?

choices.explanation: Correct. SEC rules prohibit this.
Disclosure doesn't cure it.
It impairs independence.

choices.text: No effect if the services are allowed
choices.explanation: The pay link is the problem.

mcqs.explanation: An audit partner may not earn compensation based on selling non-audit services to the audit client.

mcqs.stem: How does the public learn the name of the engagement partner on an issuer audit?

choices.explanation: That reports current events.
Correct. The firm files it.
That shows fees, not partners.
That isn't public.

mcqs.explanation: Firms file Form AP with the PCAOB to disclose the engagement partner and other participating firms.

mcqs.stem: How long may a lead audit partner serve an issuer before rotating off?

choices.explanation: That's for other partners.
Correct. Then a 5-year time-out.
That period is too short.
That period is too long.

mcqs.explanation: Lead and concurring partners rotate after 5 years, with a 5-year time-out.

mcqs.stem: Before an audit team member may join an issuer client in a financial reporting oversight role, what cooling-off period applies?

choices.explanation: That is not the rule.
That is not the rule.
Correct. SOX imposes a 1-year cooling-off.
That is not the rule.

mcqs.explanation: An issuer's CEO, CFO or similar can't have been on its audit team during the 1-year cooling-off period.

mcqs.stem: Which service may an issuer's auditor not provide?

choices.explanation: Permitted with approval.
It is an audit-related service.
It is an audit-related service.
Correct. SOX prohibits it.

mcqs.explanation: SOX bars bookkeeping, systems design, appraisal, internal audit outsourcing and other services for issuer audit clients.

mcqs.stem: A firm wants to provide permissible tax services to an issuer audit client. What is required?

choices.explanation: Correct. All services need pre-approval.
That is not required.
That is not required.
Pre-approval is required.

mcqs.explanation: The audit committee must pre-approve all audit and permissible non-audit services.

mcqs.stem: An audit partner is paid for selling non-audit services to the partner's audit client. What is the effect?

choices.explanation: It's prohibited.
Correct. SEC rules prohibit it.
That is not allowed.
That is not allowed.

mcqs.explanation: An audit partner can't earn compensation from selling non-audit services to the partner's audit clients.

mcqs.stem: A former audit manager becomes the issuer's CFO 8 months after the last audit's start. Is the firm independent?

choices.explanation: Cooling-off applies.
Disclosure does not cure it.
Correct. The 1-year cooling-off isn't met.

choices.text: Only if the manager was junior
choices.explanation: Managers count.

mcqs.explanation: Independence is impaired if a team member takes a financial reporting oversight role before the cooling-off period ends.

mcqs.stem: A firm charges an issuer audit client a contingent fee for tax planning. What is the effect?

choices.explanation: It's prohibited.
That is not allowed.
That is not allowed.
Correct. Contingent fees are prohibited.

mcqs.explanation: PCAOB and SEC rules prohibit contingent fees for any services to an audit client.

mcqs.stem: For an issuer audit client, which service is permitted if pre-approved by the audit committee?

choices.text: Bookkeeping services for a small foreign subsidiary
choices.explanation: Bookkeeping is prohibited.

choices.text: A fairness opinion on a proposed merger
choices.explanation: Fairness opinions are prohibited.
Correct. Tax compliance is permitted with pre-approval and subject to PCAOB Rules 3521–3524.

choices.text: Serving as the issuer's broker-dealer on an offering
choices.explanation: Broker-dealer services are prohibited.

mcqs.explanation: Tax compliance is permitted with pre-approval and subject to PCAOB Rules 3521–3524.

mcqs.stem: Under the SEC rules, how long must a former audit engagement team member wait before becoming the issuer's chief accounting officer without impairing the firm's independence?

choices.explanation: Correct. The one-year cooling-off period.
Two years is the time-out for other audit partners.
Five years is the lead partner time-out.
A cooling-off period applies.

mcqs.explanation: SOX Section 206: the one-year cooling-off period for financial reporting oversight roles.

mcqs.stem: Which party must pre-approve all audit and permitted nonaudit services for an issuer?

choices.explanation: Correct. SOX Section 202.
Management can't pre-approve auditor services.
The PCAOB doesn't pre-approve engagements.

choices.text: The shareholders at the annual meeting
choices.explanation: Shareholders ratify the auditor but don't pre-approve services.

mcqs.explanation: SOX Section 202.

mcqs.stem: Under GAO Government Auditing Standards, which is required when the auditor provides a nonaudit service to an audited government?

choices.text: The auditor must obtain PCAOB approval for the service
choices.explanation: The PCAOB has no role.

choices.text: Nothing, if the service fee is under $10,000
choices.explanation: There's no dollar exemption.

choices.text: Confirm management's SKE and document the threat evaluation
choices.explanation: Correct. The Yellow Book requires evaluating threats and management's SKE and documenting the evaluation.

choices.text: The auditor must also prepare the government's financial statements
choices.explanation: Not required and may be a significant threat.

mcqs.explanation: The Yellow Book requires evaluating threats and management's SKE and documenting the evaluation.

mcqs.stem: For an issuer audit client, which non-audit service may the auditor provide with audit committee preapproval?

choices.text: Bookkeeping and preparing the client's financial statements
choices.explanation: Bookkeeping is a prohibited service for issuer audit clients.

choices.text: Designing and implementing its financial information system
choices.explanation: Financial information systems design is prohibited.

choices.text: Routine tax compliance services for the company
choices.explanation: Correct. Tax compliance is permitted with preapproval (excluding aggressive tax positions and services to people in financial reporting oversight roles).

choices.text: Internal audit outsourcing related to accounting controls
choices.explanation: Internal audit outsourcing is prohibited.

mcqs.explanation: SEC Rule 2-01 and SOX §201 prohibit services such as bookkeeping, systems design, valuation, internal audit outsourcing, management functions and legal services; tax services may be provided with preapproval.

mcqs.stem: Under SEC rules, how long may the lead audit partner on an issuer audit serve before rotating off, and how long is the time-out?

choices.text: Seven years on, then two years off
choices.explanation: Seven-on, two-off applies to other audit partners.

choices.text: Three years on, then one year off
choices.explanation: No such rule applies to the lead partner.

choices.text: Ten years on, then three years off
choices.explanation: The SEC limit is five years.

choices.text: Five years on, then five years off
choices.explanation: Correct. Lead and concurring partners rotate after five consecutive years, with a five-year time-out.

mcqs.explanation: SEC Rule 2-01(c)(6): the lead and concurring partners rotate after five years with a five-year time-out; other audit partners after seven years with a two-year time-out.

mcqs.stem: Under PCAOB Rule 3526, a registered firm must communicate with an issuer's audit committee about independence:

choices.text: Only when a relationship actually impairs independence
choices.explanation: Communication is required even when independence isn't impaired.

choices.text: Only once, when the engagement is first accepted
choices.explanation: Annual communication is required.

choices.text: Before the initial engagement and annually
choices.explanation: Correct. The firm describes relationships that may bear on independence and affirms its independence.

choices.text: Only if the audit committee requests it in writing
choices.explanation: The communication is required, not optional.

mcqs.explanation: PCAOB Rule 3526 requires written communication of relationships that may reasonably be thought to bear on independence, before accepting the initial engagement and annually, and discussion with the audit committee.

mcqs.stem: A senior manager on an issuer's audit team leaves the firm to become the issuer's controller, a financial reporting oversight role. Under SEC rules, the firm's independence is impaired unless:

choices.text: The person repays any capital owed by the firm within 30 days
choices.explanation: Capital settlement matters, but the cooling-off period still applies.

choices.text: The audit committee approves the hire in advance
choices.explanation: Approval doesn't satisfy the cooling-off rule.

choices.text: Three years have passed since the person joined the firm
choices.explanation: The test is time since the person was on the audit, not since joining.

choices.text: One year has passed since the person's audit work
choices.explanation: Correct. The cooling-off period for financial reporting oversight roles is one year.

mcqs.explanation: SEC Rule 2-01(c)(2)(iii): independence is impaired if a former audit team member takes a financial reporting oversight role within one year after participating in the audit.

flashcards.back: No mutual or conflicting interest; don't audit own work; no management functions; no advocacy.

Bookkeeping; FIS design/implementation; appraisal and valuation; actuarial; internal audit outsourcing; management functions; HR; broker-dealer and investment adviser services; legal; expert services unrelated to the audit.
Lead and concurring: 5 years on, 5 off. Other audit partners: 7 on, 2 off.
1 year before a former audit team member may take a financial reporting oversight role (CEO, CFO, controller, CAO).
No tax services to persons in a financial reporting oversight role at the issuer (or their immediate family).
Independence from both the plan and the plan sponsor.
